ranking.note: Raised to P1 and moved up five places: a deadlock risk when consumer callbacks log is a reliability defect exactly at the kernel boundary, and the single-connection decision also gates the per-context logging series.

Raised to P1: LevelDB's exclusive process lock is the concrete reason external consumers (Electrs/Esplora) cannot read block/header data from a running node, which is the category's defining use case.
Moved up five places: it is the macro-level prerequisite for both #33847 and #30342, so it inherits their importance and must be reviewed before them.

Moved up two bands' worth of positions relative to its score because it warns of a silent validation bypass (cached fChecked across parameter sets), a correctness hazard for consumers rather than ordinary doc polish.

Lowered to P4: removing two redundant accessors is cosmetic API polish with no consumer asking for it, which the category explicitly places at P3 or below; it is the weakest claim on review time here.

inconsistencies: Direction conflict: #34775 restricts libbitcoinkernel to a single global logging connection and moves level config onto that handle, while #33847/#30342 attach connections to contexts with per-connection levels and per-context routing. These cannot both land as written; review #34775 first (it fixes a concrete deadlock) but settle the one-connection-vs-per-context question before merging either side.

Logging chain order matters: #29256 (context-aware log macros) and #33847 (connection/context API hooks) are both prerequisites of #30342 (per-context delivery); #33847 is explicitly framed as avoiding a later breaking API change, so it should be decided before downstream consumers and bindings adapt.

Three overlapping takes on fatal-error reporting across the kernel boundary: #29700 (util::Result/FlushResult returns), #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError notifications, removes translation.h), and #35646 (RFC moving runtime errors out of BlockValidationState via util::Expected). They redefine the same error surface; review #29700 first as the broadest restructuring, then #36326, and treat #35646 as the concept decision that may redirect both.
#36318 (BLOCK_INCONCLUSIVE / always-set invalid result) and #35646 both change ValidationState semantics exposed through the C API; coordinate so the kernel error enum is not reshaped twice.

#32427 is as much a block-storage/validation change as a kernel change (new WAL format, checksums, flush semantics); per the category note it likely needs splitting or dual review with validation reviewers.

#36353 is a documentation-only mitigation for a real correctness hazard (btck_Block caching fChecked across different consensus parameters); a reviewer should decide whether the API should instead prevent the bypass, which would supersede the doc patch.
result.notes: The category splits into two clusters that dominate review time: logging isolation (#34775, #33847, #29256, #30342, #36584) and fatal-error propagation across the boundary (#29700, #36326, #35646, #36318). Within each cluster the band differences reflect which PR makes the decision and which follow it. Only two PRs reach P1: the boundary deadlock fix and the storage lock that blocks external readers; both concern whether outside consumers can safely use the library at all.
